physical_mismatches.reason: Block geometry and power are missing. The paper gives no block x, y, width or height in metres and no per-block watts for the baseline fft scenario. Fig. 9 shows only a temperature heat map with block labels and a colourbar, so no complete floorplan and power table can be built without inventing values. No pinned assets were supplied (assets list is empty) and the GitHub repository is described as still being released.

The scenario is a 3-layer core-plus-memory 3D stack with a passive heat sink. A 2.5D chiplet placement on an interposer (RLPlanner Ascend910 or ATPlace2.5D) cannot reproduce it, so 3D inter-layer coupling and vertical heat flow are mismatched.

Cooling mismatch. The baseline uses a passive heat sink with no microfluidic cooling, but the paper's main contribution is microfluidic cooling with vertical and 90-degree bent channel patterns in case studies 2a/2b. The baseline observable does not represent those cases.

Solver and power-model mismatch. The paper's power comes from gem5 + McPAT + CACTI-3DD, with per-benchmark and per-unit microarchitectural activity, and temperatures from HotSpot 7.0. A Studio solver with its own package and materials will not reproduce 395.52 K. The paper does not publish the HotSpot material, package or heat-sink parameters needed for calibration.

No optimizer, controller, transient behaviour or reliability analysis is in the baseline scenario. The run is steady-state only, and the paper has no power time series, so transient or controller comparison is not possible.
